title: Best AI Receptionist for Contractors — If You Must
meta: The honest best-AI-receptionist guide for contractors in 2026: the least-bad picks (Smith.ai, Rosie, Goodcall), who each actually fits, and why most small shops should spend $30, not $300.
dek: Everybody ranking “best AI receptionist” is getting paid to send you to one. We'll tell you the truth first: most one- and two-truck shops shouldn't buy any of them yet. But if you're set on it, here's the honest pecking order and who each one actually fits.
verdict_text: The honest ranking: Smith.ai (most reliable — human backup), Rosie (cheapest honest entry), Goodcall (easiest to build, real limits). But read this first: for most small shops the right answer is none of them yet — missed-call text-back plus a fast human callback beats every bot for ~$30/mo and never phantom-books a job.

blocks.h: Read this before you pick one
blocks.html: AI receptionists fail in documented ways — phantom bookings (the bot says you're booked, nothing hits the calendar), hallucinated prices, and silent lost leads. We cover that in full in Is an AI Receptionist Worth It? The short version: for a small shop, the lost-job cost of one phantom booking usually dwarfs what you'd save. If that changed your mind, good. If you still want one, here's the honest field.

faq.q: What's the best AI receptionist for contractors in 2026?
faq.a: Of the AI options, Smith.ai is the most reliable because it's a hybrid — real humans escalate when the AI is out of its depth, so you get far fewer phantom bookings. Rosie is the cheapest honest entry, and Goodcall is the easiest to set up. But for most one- and two-truck shops, the best answer is still none of them — missed-call text-back plus a fast human callback is cheaper and more reliable.

faq.q: Should a small contractor use an AI receptionist at all?
faq.a: Usually not first. The documented failure modes (phantom bookings, hallucinated info) quietly cost small shops jobs they never hear about. Fix your own fast call response with missed-call text-back (~$30/mo) first; consider an AI (ideally a human-backed hybrid) only if you genuinely can't staff the phones and you test it hard.

Rosie starts at $49/mo for answering (booking requires the $149 Scale tier). Goodcall is $79/mo priced per unique caller. Smith.ai has a free 25-call tier but bills per call after that, so the cheapest headline isn't always the cheapest in practice.
